domains.title: Dashboards, reports and KPIs
domains.route: Project Overview / Costs & Contracts > Reports; Company > Reports
domains.observed: JAKH separates approved commitments, posted cost, certified gross and posted billing. The dashboard states physical progress is weighted by original WBS budget; financial progress uses certified gross / revised contract value; CPI/SPI use earned value. Reports expose source records, unallocated cost and approved forecasts. Company cash-flow policy and forecast registers were empty in the sample; that does not prove the feature is absent.
domains.current: Partial: Builder has a deterministic cost report with project/company scope, findings and CSV export. Its amounts come from seeded cost_items snapshots. It has no transaction-derived ledger, approved forecast versions, scheduling, configurable dashboards, earned-value engine or the other JAKH reports.
domains.preserve: Keep metric definitions, cutoff, company/currency, record states, cost allocation and source drill-down. Recompute ratios from numerator/denominator populations. Distinguish posted cash from bank clearance. Use the latest approved forecast at the cutoff, retaining earlier versions. Each report needs its own findings rules and export.
domains.data: Report definitions; source fact type/ID/date; metric versions; approved forecasts and snapshots; WBS/location allocation; cash-flow policies; saved filters and dashboard definitions; subscriptions and share permissions.
domains.verify: Report joins, permission filters, reversal handling, snapshot dates, policy approval, scheduler and share-token behaviour remain untested in JAKH. No full report-result reconciliation or JAKH data import has occurred.
domains.example: For one work item: revised budget 110,000; incurred 60,000; cash 45,000; remaining work 48,000; forecast 108,000; headroom 2,000. The report must explain the 15,000 cost/cash difference and never add total commitments to incurred cost. This is a proposed acceptance fixture, not a JAKH transaction.

domains.title: Approvals and personal work
domains.route: My Work > Approvals / Tasks; context on every record
domains.observed: JAKH records technical, commercial and finance certificate review stages, submission cycles, reviewer/time/decision/note, and frozen quantities at finance approval. Contract policy describes optional independent people; role-based stages alone may allow one person with several roles. Role previews change menu access.
domains.current: Partial: purchase-request draft/submit/return/approve, independent approver, membership limit, optimistic version check and append-only request events. My Work also displays synthetic records. No configurable cross-module approval policy, delegation, escalations or general task service.
domains.preserve: Route by company, document type, value, risk and role; show current owner, stage, deadline and reason. Snapshot policies per submission. Changing the approved version invalidates downstream authority as policy requires. Separate queue visibility from permission to decide.
domains.data: Policies/versions; stages; approvers; limits/currency basis; substitutes; submission cycles; decisions; task links; reminders; audit actors and timestamps.
domains.verify: Verify each source workflow separately: required roles, independence setting, returns, cancellation, delegation and locked-state edits. Do not generalise request approval into certificate or financial posting approval.
domains.example: A returned certificate keeps cycle 1. Correcting quantity starts cycle 2; only its current version can be approved. An authorised substitute can act with a recorded delegation, while the original requester cannot self-approve where independence is required.

domains.observed: Pipeline was inspected; navigation includes opportunities, activities, quotations, teams, customers, forecasts, lead/pipeline/activity reports and stage/lost-reason configuration. The full conversion and forecast rules were not tested.

domains.preserve: Preserve customer/opportunity identity, bid deadlines, activities, ownership, stage history, probability definitions, lost reasons and quotation/estimate links. Bid/no-bid decision records risks, authority and rationale.
domains.data: Leads/opportunities; customer contacts; teams; stage histories; activities; qualification documents; lost reasons; quotations and tender links.
domains.verify: Confirm duplicate lead handling, currencies, weighted forecast method, stage gates and opportunity-to-estimate-to-quotation mapping.
domains.example: A tower invitation closes on 15 November. The estimator sees one bid case with deadline, client, risk decision, documents and estimates; losing the bid preserves its priced versions and reason.

domains.title: Estimating, BOQ and tender handover
domains.route: Tenders > Estimate > BOQ / Pricing / Versions / Handover
domains.observed: Estimate EST/2026/00004 has BOQ/assemblies, building quantities, study versions, parent BOQ/share fields, direct cost, indirect allocation, overhead, profit, item/header markup, currency and approval history. Its visible pricing basis is direct plus proportional indirect, then overhead, profit and legacy markup. Handover links quotation and project; WBS budgets remain draft.
domains.current: Synthetic tender examples; no workbook intake, assembly/resource model, repeated-building quantity engine, version lock, pricing calculation or award handover.
domains.preserve: Preserve source workbook provenance, row codes, parent/child BOQ, units, assembly resources, building-specific quantities and variants, pricing sequence and precision. Approved studies lock; revisions remain distinct. Award produces linked draft commercial and budget records without silently releasing them.
domains.data: Workbook/row mappings; estimate headers; BOQ groups/lines; assembly components; rates and dates; location quantities; indirect pools; pricing order; versions; approvals; quotation/project/WBS crosswalk.
domains.verify: Verify import validation, parent caps/shares, repeated-building exceptions, resource conversion, rounding and exact markup order with saved examples. Inspect hidden detail forms before implementing formulas.
domains.example: Ten typical floors and two modified floors share an assembly. Reprice steel without overwriting the accepted tender; compare the new version, approve it, and hand over exact location quantities and the approved budget basis.

domains.title: Sales quotations and orders

domains.current: No sales quote/order model, pricing catalogue, acceptance workflow or invoice linkage. Tender examples do not implement these functions.
domains.preserve: Carry estimate version, exclusions, quantities, currency, validity, tax basis, terms and acceptance into an order and client contract. Templates, price rules, customer history and amendment authority remain accessible.
domains.data: Quotes/orders/lines; estimate revision; customers; products/pricelists; validity/terms/taxes; acceptance; templates; invoice and contract links.
domains.verify: Confirm quotation revision policy, order confirmation, cancellation, invoicing basis, payment settings and whether repeated product/customer menus open the same records.
domains.example: The accepted tower quote creates one linked order and contract. A revised offer remains visibly separate until accepted; the original approved estimate and offer remain readable.

domains.title: Projects, mobilisation and location structure

domains.observed: Project links budgets, contracts, requisitions, site materials, service entries, certificates, variations, final accounts and award estimate. Construction setup has an accounting cost centre and structured buildings/floors/zones with code, kind and parent. Direct-award and completed projects exist.
domains.current: Partial read scope: projects have ID, company, name, code, a flat location string and phase. No project creation/setup workflow, hierarchy, accounting cost centre, templates, task lifecycle or role administration.
domains.preserve: Create a project from award or direct award; one owning company, stable WBS/BOQ/location/system dimensions, responsible team, baseline approvals and readiness checks. Location hierarchy must support tower > floor > unit and cross-location systems without repeated free text.
domains.data: Projects; customer/contract links; location tree; WBS; cost centre; phase/history; roles; templates; tasks/dependencies; tags; setup checklist and baseline approvals.
domains.verify: Inspect set-up gates, task billing/margin rules, project closure/reopening, hierarchy changes and project-specific access. Preserve linked records when moving or renaming locations.
domains.example: Open Tower A > Floor 12 > Unit 1204 once. Its drawings, work quantities, NCRs, material issues, costs and snags resolve to the same structured location.

domains.title: Requisition, sourcing and purchase orders
domains.route: Project > Buying > Requests / Sourcing / Orders & deliveries; Company > Buying
domains.observed: JAKH requisition has requested lines, restricted pricing, project/WBS, contract line, location, material-demand reference, required date and reservation/cancellation. Visible text says approved tax-exclusive company-currency prices reserve released WBS budget. Linked PO P00005 exposes received/billed quantities and receipt/bill links.
domains.current: Partial only at request: one line per request; vendor holds one price/quote/currency rather than product-specific quote lines; decimal arithmetic, repricing and approval work. There are no RFQs, supplier offers, agreements, PO lines, receipts/bills or reservation ledger. No completed procurement chain.
domains.preserve: Capture multi-line demand without forcing a vendor; compare product/quantity/UOM-specific quotes, lead time, tax/freight and validity. Use approved company-currency reservations with release/replacement rules. Split orders by legal company/vendor/currency. Track partial receipt, rejection, returns, billing and cancellation separately.
domains.data: Demand; requisitions/lines; reservations; products/UOM; RFQs/offers/lines; agreement terms; approved quote/rate snapshots; PO versions/lines; receipt/bill links and source quantities.
domains.verify: JAKH procurement sample is company-currency based; vendor-currency defaults are a requested enhancement, not proven parity. Verify overspend policy, reserved-to-committed handoff, partial cancellation, overreceipt and 3-way matching.
domains.example: Request 100 units; award 60 in USD and 40 in AED to different vendors; create linked orders. Receive 30 and reject 5. Only accepted receipts can support the appropriate bill; remaining demand, reservations and FX snapshots stay traceable.

domains.title: WBS, budgets and cost control
domains.route: Project > Plan > Work & budget; Costs & Contracts > Cost control / Forecasts
domains.observed: WBS has parent, code, project/company/currency, cost code, budget and release state. Budget revisions have a separate destination. An editable WBS Forecast Amount of zero was not authoritative: an approved dated forecast of AED 8,428,000 existed with actual snapshot 6,324,447 and remaining uncommitted 2,103,553.
domains.current: Seeded flat cost_items contain original/revised budget, commitment, incurred, cash, forecast and request allowance. No WBS hierarchy, budget revisions/release, transaction allocation, resource breakdown, approved forecast history or actual-to-ledger reconciliation.
domains.preserve: Original budget never changes; approved revisions build revised budget. Keep reservation, commitment, received exposure/accrual, posted actual, cash and forecast distinct. Allocate costs by work item/location/resource/period; make unallocated visible. Forecast equals actual plus remaining committed plus remaining uncommitted plus risk, each counted once.
domains.data: WBS tree; BOQ/WBS/location crosswalk; original and revised budgets; release/approvals; source cost facts; accrual/reversal links; allocations; approved forecast versions and dates; remaining-cost detail.
domains.verify: Confirm budget authority/overrun behaviour, accrual clearing, price/quantity variances, stock-consumption versus purchase timing, labour/plant rates and forecast selection at historical cutoffs.
domains.example: A late supplier bill replaces an earlier accrual for the same work; actual cost does not double. Revising Floor 12 budget changes the approved revision, while the original tower estimate remains unchanged.

domains.title: Materials, stores, returns and waste
domains.route: Project > Site > Materials & waste; Company > Stores
domains.observed: Requisition/PO/receipt links and stock source records were recorded. Stores navigation includes transfers, stocktake, scrap, replenishment, moves and returns. Scrap form exposes product, quantity/UOM, reason, company and replenishment; full waste handling was not proven.
domains.current: Read-only materials/waste/stores examples. No stock ledger, warehouse/location model, receiving, issue/return, reservation, valuation, count adjustment or waste authorisation engine.
domains.preserve: Separate ordered, received, quarantined, available, issued, returned, reused and scrapped quantities. Each movement carries source/destination, project/item/location, actor, date and valuation. Waste needs cause, approval, reuse/disposal destination, carrier/evidence and cost treatment.
domains.data: Products/UOM/conversions; warehouses/bins; batches/serials where used; opening stock/valuation; receipt/transfer/issue/return/scrap lines; reservations; stocktakes; disposal evidence and linked NCR.
domains.verify: Verify valuation method, negative-stock policy, partial/rejected receipt, return-to-supplier credit, physical counts, lot/serial requirements and waste cost recognition. Treat specialist environmental requirements as requirements to confirm, not observed JAKH logic.
domains.example: Receive 100 tiles; issue 80; return 5; scrap 3 from issued stock with approval. Preserve the balance and cost provenance, with the NCR linked to the same loss rather than charging it twice.

domains.title: Site diaries, labour and plant actuals
domains.route: Project > Site > Daily work / Resources; Plan > Look-ahead
domains.observed: Site diary contains manpower, equipment, photos, work/events and review context. Separate allocation and actual-feed destinations exist. Project-control facts distinguish native workflow and validated integration sources.
domains.current: Read-only daily-work examples, with no diary editing, attendance allocation, resource booking, approvals or source-feed ingestion.
domains.preserve: Keep planned allocation distinct from accepted actual hours/quantities. Diary evidence records location/work/date/weather/events; approved time and plant use feed costs once. Integration replays must not duplicate actuals.
domains.data: Daily diaries; work quantities; worker/crew/equipment identities; allocation and actual lines; rates; evidence; approvals; source-system ID/batch and corrections.
domains.verify: Verify paid versus worked hours, overtime, idle time, hired plant minimums, actual acceptance and correction/reversal rules; confirm source systems and ownership.
domains.example: A crane planned for eight hours works five and is idle three due to missing drawings. Record both with cause, attach diary evidence and allocate approved cost to the correct work package once.

domains.title: Client contract, measured BOQ and certification
domains.route: Project > Costs & Contracts > Client contract / Claims & certificates / Changes
domains.observed: JAKH has immutable client BOQ in company currency, original/revised contract values, BOQ revisions, building budgets, finance policy and staged certificate approval. Certificates take cumulative installed quantities, derive previous/current/remaining, include approved owner variations and calculate retention/recovery/deductions. Finance approval freezes quantities; linked draft invoice remains separately controlled.
domains.current: No contract/BOQ/certificate domain or calculations. Payments and change examples cannot measure, review, certify, revise BOQ or create a linked invoice.
domains.preserve: Separate claimed, technically accepted, commercially reviewed, certified, invoiced, due, paid and cleared. Snapshot contract rates/quantities and approved variation entitlement at cutoff. Enforce cumulative limits and explicit corrections; preserve previous approved periods and review cycles.
domains.data: Contract header/finance terms; original/revised BOQ/locations; unit rates; certificate periods/lines; previous/current/cumulative quantities; deductions; approval route/cycles; invoice/credit links.
domains.verify: Verify overmeasurement, negative corrections, simultaneous certificates, tax/deduction bases, approvals by different people, invoice idempotency and prior-period credit adjustments. Review actual BOQ-revision forms before defining migration columns.
domains.example: Previously certified 40 m3; cumulative accepted 55 m3; current period is 15 m3. Returning the submission must not change the approved 40. One approved certificate can generate only the intended invoice, even after a retry.

domains.title: Advances, retention, securities and final accounts
domains.route: Costs & Contracts > Advances / Retention / Securities / Final account; Handover > Closeout
domains.observed: Client contract links advances/retention and final accounts; visible policy warns an advance ceiling is not cash receipt. Approved final account records certified gross, recovered advance, released retention and approval metadata. A close-contract/project action exists but was not executed. Guarantees have a navigation destination.
domains.current: Read-only payment/closeout examples. No advance balances, retention caps/releases, guarantee lifecycle, final-account reconciliation or controlled closure.
domains.preserve: Track actual advance receipt/payment separately from contractual entitlement; recover only according to terms and outstanding balance. Release retention/securities against milestones and authority. Technical handover, defect obligations and financial closure stay separate.
domains.data: Advance/recovery entries; retention accrual/releases; guarantees/bonds and expiries; final account versions; accepted adjustments; disputes; releases; closure/reopening events and obligations.
domains.verify: Verify deduction caps, partial release, foreign-currency advances, bond renewals/calls, outstanding liabilities and closeout blockers. A completed-project sample does not prove all closure checks.
domains.example: A floor is accepted while the tower retains defects and an unrecovered advance. Allow partial handover; block unsupported final settlement or release and clearly show the remaining obligations.

domains.title: Subcontract package through settlement
domains.route: Project > Buying > Subcontracts > Package; Costs & Contracts views link the same package
domains.observed: Service entry records PO line, project/WBS/contract line/location and completed work; visible rule says approval creates received-cost exposure and supplier invoice cannot exceed approved service quantity. Supplier certificate links service entry, agreement, retention/recovery and bill. Agreement has retention percent/cap/accounts, advance/recovery terms and balances. Eight linked certificates were visible.
domains.current: Read-only package/application/certificate examples. No tender award, order amendment, measured service approval, quantity ceiling, deduction engine, payable or settlement workflow.
domains.preserve: One package holds scope/BOQ, subcontractor, award/order, revisions, applications, accepted measurements, certificates, deductions, bills, payments and balance. Requested, accepted and certified quantities differ. Correct previously accepted work via traceable adjustment; never overwrite paid history.
domains.data: Package/award/PO lines; applications and claimed quantities; service entries and acceptance; amendments; corrections; finance agreements; certificates/deductions; bills/credits/payments; guarantees and closeout.
domains.verify: Verify amendment authority, overmeasurement, disputed quantities, backcharges, retention caps, advance recovery, bill limits, correction/reversal and settlement gates. Menus alone do not verify those exceptions.
domains.example: Claim 120 m2, accept 100, return 20 with reason. At AED 200/m2, gross is 20,000; a 10% retention is 2,000 before tax/other agreed deductions. The bill and subsequent correction retain links to approved measurements.

domains.title: Programme, progress and delay
domains.route: Project > Plan > Programme / Look-ahead / Constraints / Delay events
domains.observed: JAKH declares Primavera P6 as schedule master; accepted WBS progress contributes planned/earned value. Sample progress can be manual and some activity/location/finish links were blank. A full critical-path or EOT engine was not proven.
domains.current: Programme/KPI examples only; no activity/dependency/calendar model, baseline import, progress approval, schedule update or delay assessment.
domains.preserve: Declare master per project; preserve baseline/current version, calendars, activity/WBS/location mappings, data date, progress basis and acceptance. Link constraints/delay events to instructions, diaries and mitigation. Keep forecast completion separate from contractual extension entitlement.
domains.data: Schedule versions; activities/dependencies/calendars; baseline and current dates; progress snapshots; PV/EV basis; resource links; delay events/notices; evidence and accepted extensions.
domains.verify: Confirm required P6 exchange format and external ownership, accepted manual fallback, duplicate-import handling, baseline changes, float/critical-path method and delay-analysis requirements. Retaining an integration requires explicit scope treatment, not silent removal.
domains.example: A delayed drawing blocks Floor 12 concrete. The same event links RFI, diary and affected activity; show forecast slippage and mitigation while an EOT assessment remains separately reviewed.

domains.title: Finance, payments and cash
domains.route: Company > Finance; project-linked views in Costs & Contracts
domains.observed: JAKH exposes receivables/payables, journals/items, audit trail, accounting reports, taxes, chart of accounts, currencies, fiscal positions and multi-ledger. A posted customer payment had balanced bank/receivable entries and invoice reference. Posted payment evidence did not prove bank reconciliation.
domains.current: No original accounting engine, receivable/payable subledger, journals, tax/period controls, payment allocation, bank reconciliation, FX gains/losses or financial statements. The cost report and payment examples are not accounting.
domains.preserve: Build original double-entry accounting with company periods/numbering, immutable posting and authorised reversals. Reconcile AP/AR, advances, retention, stock/project costs, cash and bank. Keep operational certificates separate from legal invoices. Preserve currencies, rates and settlement differences.
domains.data: COA/journals/taxes/periods; invoice/bill lines; open items; credit notes; journal entries/items; payment allocations; bank statements/reconciliations; exchange rates; control-account links and analytic allocation.
domains.verify: Source posting rules, localisations, tax treatment, lock dates, currencies and multi-ledger purpose need validation. The demo is not the production accounting migration source. No opening balance, trial balance, AP/AR or bank reconciliation has been imported.
domains.example: A USD supplier bill is booked at one rate and partially paid at another. Record remaining USD liability, company-currency cash and realised FX separately; settle only the approved payment and reconcile the bank independently.

Snag links location, WBS/BOQ and contractor.
domains.current: Read-only NCR, drawing, RFI and snag examples. No controlled revision workflow, attachment storage, review routing, ITP holds, NCR verification or closure/reopening.
domains.preserve: Keep NCR requirement/inspection, containment, root cause, disposition/remedy, responsible party, evidence, independent verification and closure/reopen. Connect cost, waste, change and delay consequences. Documents require unique identity plus revision, issue purpose, supersession, distributions and review history; approval is distinct from current/issued-for-construction.
domains.data: Quality/HSE cases; severity/type; requirement/inspection reference; remedies/verifications; attachments/photos; document identities/revisions/hashes; review cycles/transmittals; snag locations and acceptance.
domains.verify: Confirm source NCR transition requirements, HSE reporting/restrictions, review routing and enforcement of superseded drawings/hold points. The external NCR-kit reference was contextual; no kit was purchased/imported and its content is not proof of JAKH capability.
domains.example: Concrete fails inspection. Open one NCR, contain work, approve a remedy, attach retest evidence and verify closure. Link rework cost/waste/delay without duplicate cases. Workers must find the correct approved drawing revision for that location.
